seal.statement: A claim that cannot be proved until its head is published has a lifecycle instead of a dead end. Landing required a green doneWhen and landing produced the head, so a quest whose evidence is hosted runs on a published tree could never close; its own parent recorded that the more rigorous sealing was the one the machinery punished. A quest may now declare that its claim needs a published head, and optionally what proving its implementation means. Landing such a quest measures the implementation rather than the claim and leaves it awaiting external proof, a state it carries and never a terminal one; the quest stays open until something measures the sealed claim and records the exact head that proof certifies. The closure may live on a later head, but which tree was actually proven is never left to inference. The case is generic and additive: it is not a mode for one kind of evidence, and a quest that proves its claim locally still closes in one step with nothing about it changed.

text: Added the lifecycle case rather than a mode for one kind of evidence. A quest declares externalProof when its claim needs a published head, and may declare implementedWhen for what proving its implementation means; landing such a quest measures the implementation and records awaiting-external-proof, a status the quest carries and that TERMINAL_STATUSES deliberately excludes, so the quest stays open. note --externally-proven measures the sealed doneWhen and records the exact implementation head the proof certifies, so a closure living on a later head never leaves which tree was proven to inference. Nothing in it names a workflow, a runner or a provider. A quest that proves its claim locally is untouched: five scenarios include one asserting exactly that, and one asserting a hold is not cleared by waiting on a head. The hosted-gate frontier that recorded this circularity now declares externalProof, and its closing path already refuses correctly, naming the claim rather than the machinery.
